system:
You are an expert at writing C programs that trigger memory safety bugs.

Given a vulnerability description and source code, write a standalone C program that triggers the bug. The program should:

1. Include necessary headers
2. Set up data structures to reach the vulnerable code path
3. Call the vulnerable function with crafted input that triggers the bug
4. Be compilable as: clang -fsanitize=address -g -O0 reproducer.c -o reproducer

The reproducer must be SELF-CONTAINED. It can:
- Re-declare types and function signatures as needed
- Use the project's public API functions
- Provide stub implementations for internal functions

Respond with a JSON object:
{
  "reproducer_code": "// C code here",
  "compile_flags": ["-I/path/if/needed"],
  "explanation": "how this triggers the bug"
}

Generate a standalone C reproducer that triggers this vulnerability:

File: bfd/coff-sh.c
Line: 884
Function: sh_relax_section
Bug type: out-of-bounds-read
CWE: CWE-125
Explanation: Reads a 32-bit value with bfd_get_32 at contents + (paddr - sec->vma) after only verifying paddr < sec->size. If paddr > sec->size - 4, this reads past the end of the section buffer.

Source context:
```c

      845: 			     + (irelfn->r_symndx
      846: 				* bfd_coff_symesz (abfd))),
      847: 			    &sym);

      850: 	  _bfd_error_handler
      851: 	    /* xgettext: c-format */
      852: 	    (_("%pB: %#" PRIx64 ": warning: symbol in unexpected section"),
      853: 	     abfd, (uint64_t) paddr);
      854: 	  continue;
      855: 	}
      856: 
      857:       if (sym.n_sclass != C_EXT)
      858: 	{

      860: 		    - sec->vma
      861: 		    + sec->output_section->vma
      862: 		    + sec->output_offset);
      863: 	}
      864:       else

      871: 	      && h->root.type != bfd_link_hash_defweak)

      874: 		 symbol.  Just ignore it--it will be caught by the

      880: 		    + h->root.u.def.section->output_section->vma
      881: 		    + h->root.u.def.section->output_offset);
      882: 	}

>>>   884:       symval += bfd_get_32 (abfd, contents + paddr - sec->vma);
      885:

      887:       foff = (symval
      888: 	      - (irel->r_vaddr
      889: 		 - sec->vma
      890: 		 + sec->output_section->vma
      891: 		 + sec->output_offset
      892: 		 + 4));
      893:       if (foff < -0x1000 || foff >= 0x1000)

      899:       /* Shorten the function call.  */

      901:       /* For simplicity of coding, we are going to modify the section
      902: 	 contents, the section relocs, and the BFD symbol table.  We
      903: 	 must tell the rest of the code not to free up this
      904: 	 information.  It would be possible to instead create a table
      905: 	 of changes which have to be made, as is done in coff-mips.c;
      906: 	 that would be more work, but would require less memory when
      907: 	 the linker is run.  */

      910:       coff_section_data (abfd, sec)->contents = contents;

      916:       irel->r_type = R_SH_PCDISP;

      923: 	  bfd_put_16 (abfd,
      924: 		      (bfd_vma) 0xb000 | ((foff >> 1) & 0xfff),
```
